items.t: Fairfield Island is a residential neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack, BC, north of Chilliwack Proper.

Planning identity: the City's Official Community Plan page lists "B2 - Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan" as a Schedule B plan — Fairfield Island is a named neighbourhood-plan area grouped with Chilliwack Proper, inside the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500. The Sardis plan is Schedule B5 and the Agricultural Plan is Schedule B1 of the same bylaw — never "Schedule D / Bylaw 5024."
Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. Nearby area: Chilliwack Proper to the south, with which it shares the Schedule B2 neighbourhood plan.
Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not — states the apartment-condo zero plainly.
The City plans the area (Schedule B2, with Chilliwack Proper).

A detached house here can still come with a strata fee. The Williams Road example sits in a 6-unit bare-land strata described in its listing as carrying a minimal fee — a buyer who assumes "detached = no strata" misses the corporation, its bylaws and its Form B entirely.
The flood question is open. A seller's reassurance is not a substitute for the City's own parcel check.

The plan pairing surprises people: Fairfield Island is not planned on its own — its neighbourhood plan is the joint Schedule B2 "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan," so plan searches run under only "Fairfield Island" miss documents filed under Chilliwack Proper.

Provincial dates that changed a bare-land strata lot's rule book here: rental bylaws void November 24, 2022; wider 55+ exemptions May 1, 2023; 10% CRF minimum November 1, 2023; depreciation reports every five years from July 1, 2024; Chilliwack SSMUH Bylaw 5395 adopted June 18, 2024.

items.t: Board identity and numbers: Chilliwack is a CADREB market, not a Fraser Valley or Greater Vancouver board market, and is not covered by SnapStats, so SnapStats figures do not apply to this area.

Chilliwack property taxes (city ground only): notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1; a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026. Fairfield Island is inside the City of Chilliwack, so the city scheme applies — the FVRD electoral-area rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, 5% after July 2 + 5% after Oct 31) does not apply here; never mix the two.

The "island" is a slough, not the Fraser River, that makes it an island in daily life. The Schedule B-2 plan states Fairfield Island is separated from the rest of Chilliwack Proper by the Hope Slough, is currently accessible only via road bridges at Menzies and Young Roads, and will add a planned pedestrian and cyclist bridge at Williams Street — every trip to the hospital and the downtown stock crosses one of those two bridges.

The plan expects infill, not a townhouse project. The Schedule B-2 framework addresses infill development opportunities — redevelopment of existing large lots into smaller-lot single detached, duplex or row housing, some convenience commercial, and new attached housing along Hope River Road — and notes there are limited commercial services within the neighbourhood at present.

Fairfield Island's housing era is stated in the City's own plan. The Schedule B-2 plan characterises the current building stock as predominantly one- and two-storey 1970s–1980s detached homes — a buyer here is buying a house of that era, with a house inspection to match, not a strata purchase with a depreciation report.

items.t: Development Permit Areas in the OCP's Schedule D, as named on the City page: D-1 Drinking Water Supply, D-2 Hillside Environment, D-3 Riparian Area, D-4 Farm Home Plate, D-5 Hillside Development, D-6 Downtown, D-7 Mixed-Use Areas, D-8 Residential, D-9 Commercial, D-10 Industrial.

ALR block — full form (the northern/eastern perimeter where ALR ground exists): properties in the Agricultural Land Reserve are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR regulations; ALC approval may be required before the City can approve related development applications, and the City directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap; an ALC application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, for placing fill or removing soil, for non-farm uses, and for subdivision or a boundary adjustment, with ALC applications referred to the City for review. Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: principal residence ≤500 m² total floor area; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm Home Plate: OCP Development Permit Area 4 exists to reduce the long-term impact of residential uses on agricultural land, and a Development Permit is required when the Zoning Bylaw's Farm Home Plate regulations are not met. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line is an error and is not used here.
The "island" cannot be sourced — and that itself is the detail. A buyer's flood diligence therefore starts with the City directly, not with the page.
A detached house here can still be a strata purchase. Title, not appearance, decides whether a Form B, strata fees and bylaws come with the lot.

The neighbourhood plan is shared, not standalone. Fairfield Island has no plan of its own: it is planned jointly with Chilliwack Proper as Schedule B2 of Bylaw 5500 — a buyer reading only a "Fairfield Island plan" would be reading the wrong document.

items.t: Identity: Fairfield Island is a residential neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack, north of Chilliwack Proper, working to Young Road North, Menzies Road, Hope River Road, Clare Avenue, Bell Road and Ballam Road. The City's OCP page confirms the planning identity: Schedule B2 is the "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan" — a named neighbourhood-plan area grouped with Chilliwack Proper.

The plan name does quiet work: Fairfield Island does not have its own neighbourhood plan — it is planned jointly with Chilliwack Proper under Schedule B2, so the document a buyer should read for this area covers the older city core as well, and "Fairfield Island policy" usually means a B2 passage written for both areas at once.

The perimeter is a different legal world from the interior: Two streets apart, a Fairfield Island parcel can move from flat-lot residential ground into ALR ground where a house plan triggers the Farm Home Plate permit area, the ALC residence caps and the no-stratification rule — the split is per-parcel on the City Webmap, not visible from the street.
